label: prop:skein-finiteness-bound
title: Finiteness of the nuclear chart: the Skein polynomial zero as stability boundary
html:
The finiteness inequality

Proposition. A nuclear configuration \mathcal{N}(p, n) is stable only if the Skein polynomial is positive,

  P_{\mathcal{N}(p,n)}(q)  >  0,

equivalently, for each generator i = 0, \ldots, A-2 the traced volume is positive,

  \hat{V}_i(q) = 
  c_+^{(i)}\lambda_+^{k_i}
  + 
  c_-^{(i)}\lambda_-^{k_i}
   >  0
  \qquad (i = 0, \ldots, A-2),

where \hat{V}_i = z \cdot M_{11}^{(i)} + M_{21}^{(i)} is the traced volume of generator \sigma_i (transfer matrix), P = \prod_i \hat{V}_i, the transfer-matrix eigenvalues \lambda_\pm are real and opposite in sign (\det T < 0), and k_i = A-1-i.

Although each \hat{V}_i > 0 for q > 1, the product P can flip sign through Yang--Baxter cross-terms. The sign flip is governed by the q-deformed finiteness bound

  \boxed{[A-1]_q!  >  [2]_q^{A-1}},
  \qquad
  [n]_q! = \prod_{k=1}^{n} [k]_q,
  \quad
  [k]_q = \frac{q^k - q^{-k}}{q - q^{-1}},

first satisfied at A = 5 for all q > 1; at the substrate q_0 the Skein-polynomial sign flip occurs at A = 6 (one step later, because the (2,2) shell closure stabilises A = 4). Shell closures at the magic numbers \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} re-stabilise P > 0, extending the physical nuclear chart to A \sim 300 (shell closure).

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs, real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring. Only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
